name: Function
factorsThrough_iff
result.signature: (g : α → γ) [Nonempty γ] : g.FactorsThrough f ↔ ∃ (e : β → γ), g = e ∘ f
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} (g : α → γ) [Nonempty γ],
  Function.FactorsThrough g f ↔ ∃ e, g = e ∘ f
result.value:
:=
  ⟨fun hf =>
    ⟨extend f g (const β (Classical.arbitrary γ)), funext (fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, hf.extend_apply])⟩,
    fun h _ _ hf => by rw [Classical.choose_spec h, comp_apply, comp_apply, hf]⟩
result.informal_name: Factorization Through a Function iff Existence of Intermediate Function
result.informal_description: For a function $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ with $\gamma$ non-empty, the function $g$ factors through $f$ (i.e., whenever $f(a) = f(b)$, then $g(a) = g(b)$) if and only if there exists a function $e : \beta \to \gamma$ such that $g = e \circ f$.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
result.type: {α : Sort u_1} → {β : Sort u_2} → {γ : Sort u_3} → (α → γ) → (α → β) → Prop
result.value:
:=
  ∀ ⦃a b⦄, f a = f b → g a = g b
result.informal_name: Function g factors through function f
result.informal_description: The proposition that for all $a, b$, if $f(a) = f(b)$ then $g(a) = g(b)$. This means the function $g$ respects the equivalence relation induced by $f$.

name: Set
EqOn
comp_eq
result.signature:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_7} {f : ι → α} {g₁ g₂ : α → β},
  Set.EqOn g₁ g₂ (Set.range f) → g₁ ∘ f = g₂ ∘ f
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_7} {f : ι → α} {g₁ g₂ : α → β},
  Set.EqOn g₁ g₂ (Set.range f) → g₁ ∘ f = g₂ ∘ f
result.informal_description: If two functions $ g_1 $ and $ g_2 $ are equal on the image of a function $ f $, then their compositions with $ f $ are equal, i.e., $ g_1 \circ f = g_2 \circ f $.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
extend_comp
result.signature: {g : α → γ} (e' : β → γ) (hf : FactorsThrough g f) : extend f g e' ∘ f = g
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (e' : β → γ),
  Function.FactorsThrough g f → Function.extend f g e' ∘ f = g
result.value:
:=
  funext fun a => hf.extend_apply e' a
result.informal_name: Composition of Extended Function with Original Function Recovers the Original Function
result.informal_description: If $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ factors through $f : \alpha \to \beta$ (i.e., $f(a) = f(b)$ implies $g(a) = g(b)$), then composing the extended function $\text{extend}(f, g, e') : \beta \to \gamma$ with $f$ yields the original function $g$. Formally, $\text{extend}(f, g, e') \circ f = g$.

name: Set
EqOn
comp_right
result.signature: (hg : t.EqOn g₁ g₂) (hf : s.MapsTo f t) : s.EqOn (g₁ ∘ f) (g₂ ∘ f)
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {f : α → β} {g₁ g₂ : β → γ},
  Set.EqOn g₁ g₂ t → Set.MapsTo f s t → Set.EqOn (g₁ ∘ f) (g₂ ∘ f) s
result.informal_name: Composition Preserves Equality on a Set
result.informal_description: If two functions $g_1$ and $g_2$ are equal on a set $t$, and a function $f$ maps a set $s$ into $t$, then the compositions $g_1 \circ f$ and $g_2 \circ f$ are equal on $s$.

name: Function
FactorsThrough
comp_left
result.signature: {α β γ δ : Sort*} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ} (h : FactorsThrough g f) (g' : γ → δ) : FactorsThrough (g' ∘ g) f
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {δ : Sort u_4} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ},
  Function.FactorsThrough g f → ∀ (g' : γ → δ), Function.FactorsThrough (g' ∘ g) f
result.informal_name: Composition on the Left Preserves Factorization Through
result.informal_description: If a function $g : \alpha \to \gamma$ factors through $f : \alpha \to \beta$ (i.e., $f(a) = f(b)$ implies $g(a) = g(b)$), then composing $g$ with any function $g' : \gamma \to \delta$ preserves this property: the composition $g' \circ g$ also factors through $f$.

name: Function
Coequalizer
desc
result.signature: {γ : Type*} (u : β → γ) (hu : u ∘ f = u ∘ g) : Coequalizer f g → γ
result.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  {β : Type u_2} → (f g : α → β) → {γ : Type u_3} → (u : β → γ) → u ∘ f = u ∘ g → Function.Coequalizer f g → γ
result.value:
:=
  Quot.lift u (fun _ _ (.intro e) ↦ congrFun hu e)
result.informal_description: Given a function $ u : \beta \to \gamma $ satisfying $ u \circ f = u \circ g $, there exists a function from the coequalizer of $ f $ and $ g $ to $ \gamma $ induced by $ u $.

name: Function
extend_comp
result.signature: (hf : Injective f) (g : α → γ) (e' : β → γ) : extend f g e' ∘ f = g
result.type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ (g : α → γ) (e' : β → γ), Function.extend f g e' ∘ f = g
result.value:
:=
  funext fun a ↦ hf.extend_apply g e' a
result.informal_name: Extension Composed with Injective Function Equals Original Function
result.informal_description: For an injective function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $, the composition of the function $ h : \beta \to \gamma $ defined by $ h(b) = g(a) $ if there exists an $ a \in \alpha $ with $ f(a) = b $, and $ h(b) = e'(b) $ otherwise, with $ f $, equals $ g $. That is, $ h \circ f = g $.

name: Set
EqOn
cancel_left
result.signature: (h : s.EqOn (g ∘ f₁) (g ∘ f₂)) (hg : t.InjOn g) (hf₁ : s.MapsTo f₁ t) (hf₂ : s.MapsTo f₂ t) : s.EqOn f₁ f₂
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {f₁ f₂ : α → β} {g : β → γ},
  Set.EqOn (g ∘ f₁) (g ∘ f₂) s → Set.InjOn g t → Set.MapsTo f₁ s t → Set.MapsTo f₂ s t → Set.EqOn f₁ f₂ s
result.value: := fun _ ha => hg (hf₁ ha) (hf₂ ha) (h ha)
result.informal_name: Left Cancellation of Function Composition via Injectivity on a Set
result.informal_description: If $ g \circ f_1 $ and $ g \circ f_2 $ agree on a set $ s $, $ g $ is injective on a set $ t $, and both $ f_1 $ and $ f_2 $ map $ s $ into $ t $, then $ f_1 $ and $ f_2 $ must agree on $ s $. Formally, given $ s.\text{EqOn}(g \circ f_1, g \circ f_2) $, $ t.\text{InjOn}(g) $, $ s.\text{MapsTo}(f_1, t) $, and $ s.\text{MapsTo}(f_2, t) $, it follows that $ s.\text{EqOn}(f_1, f_2) $.

name: Equiv
comp_symm_eq
result.signature: {α β γ} (e : α ≃ β) (f : β → γ) (g : α → γ) : g ∘ e.symm = f ↔ g = f ∘ e
result.type: ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} (e : α ≃ β) (f : β → γ) (g : α → γ), g ∘ ⇑e.symm = f ↔ g = f ∘ ⇑e
result.informal_name: Composition with Inverse Equivalence Characterizes Function Equality
result.informal_description: For any equivalence $ e : \alpha \simeq \beta $, function $ f : \beta \to \gamma $, and function $ g : \alpha \to \gamma $, the composition $ g \circ e^{-1} $ equals $ f $ if and only if $ g $ equals $ f \circ e $. This establishes a bijection between functions $ \beta \to \gamma $ and functions $ \alpha \to \gamma $ that commute with the equivalence $ e $.
